regulation: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 / UKCA regime
title: United Kingdom: UK-based responsible person
summary: Goods placed on the GB market by a business not established in the UK generally require a UK-established economic operator. The UK regime diverges from the EU GPSR and is assessed separately.

sources.title: General Product Safety Regulations 2005
sources.note: MAJOR FINDING, not a citation fix — flagging rather than correcting, because the correction isn't obvious. Two separate problems: (1) reg. 8 of GPSR 2005, cited here, is titled 'Obligations of distributors' per the statute's own table of contents — nothing to do with a responsible-person appointment. (2) More fundamentally: as of guidance dated February 2026 (checked via a specialist compliance guide, corroborated by the Act itself), there is NO current blanket UK Responsible Person requirement for general consumer goods. The Product Regulation and Metrology Act 2025 is an *enabling* Act — it grants government the power to create a UKRP requirement by future secondary legislation, which 'has not yet been made' per that guidance. What GPSR 2005 actually does today is narrower: where the manufacturer is not UK-established, the 'producer' duties fall to (a) a UK-established representative if the manufacturer happens to have appointed one, or failing that (b) whichever UK-established importer places the product on the GB market — there is no requirement to *appoint* anyone specifically, unlike the EU's Art. 16. A general, product-agnostic UKRP appointment duty already exists today only in specific sectors — cosmetics (its own Responsible Person regime) and medical devices (UK MDR 2002) are two confirmed examples — not for general consumer goods under GPSR. Tabeen decision needed: this requirement as titled/scoped ('United Kingdom: UK-based responsible person', jurisdiction-wide) does not appear to describe current law. Options: (a) withdraw/hold this row until PRMA 2025's secondary legislation actually lands, tracking it as a future-dated requirement; (b) rescope it to describe today's narrower importer/representative-of-last-resort rule, which is real but is a very different (and much weaker) thing to tell a customer than 'appoint a UK responsible person'; (c) split into sector-specific rows for the categories where a UKRP already is required today (cosmetics, medical devices) if those categories matter to this catalog. Given `confidence: "low"` was already set on the draft, whoever wrote it may have suspected this. NOT marked ready for sign-off — this is a scoping decision, not a read-and-sign. DECISION (Tabeen Raoof, 2026-09-20, PR #3 review): Held / Blocked, option (a) from the three above. Forcing this requirement now risks modelling phantom compliance; the correct call is to leave this row in draft until PRMA 2025's secondary legislation creating the actual UKRP duty is tabled and numbered. Re-check when that happens rather than on a fixed schedule — state stays draft deliberately, not by default.
